thread.text:
Certified is a claim. Tested to is not.

If a water filter box says NSF 42, it has been checked for chlorine and taste. Nothing else.

What the numbers actually mean:

401 covers microplastics
53 covers lead and PFAS on carbon
58 covers reverse osmosis
P473 covers PFOA and PFOS

A filter certified only to 42 tells you nothing about health contaminants.

Reverse osmosis is the only household technology that removes PFAS, microplastics, lead and fluoride. Everything else covers a subset, which is fine once you know which subset you need.

Full breakdown: https://plasticdetox.org/articles/best-water-filters.html

In May the EPA proposed keeping the 4 parts per trillion limit for PFOA and PFOS, while letting utilities push compliance from 2029 to 2031.

The same proposal would rescind the limits for GenX, PFHxS, PFNA and mixtures entirely.

The deadline moved. The contamination did not.
Reverse osmosis is the only household filter that removes PFAS, microplastics, lead and fluoride. New guide is up.
